documented_fact: State scientific-mission dossier for Sylvain Lévi's India/Japan mission. Scholarly citations identify within it Lévi's mission request to the Minister of Public Instruction, probably April 1896.
research_consequence: Creates a state-administrative route for authorization, itinerary, reports, funding and return chronology independent of Lévi's private papers.

documented_fact: Lardinois cites a letter by Sylvain Lévi from Kathmandu, 5 Feb 1898, to Foreign Minister Gabriel Hanotaux, describing his study of pandit methods and direct contact with Indian religious life.
research_consequence: Provides a precisely dated mission document inside the administrative dossier; useful for reconstructing the mission's closing sequence toward Sep 1898.

documented_fact: Archival guide identifies manuscripts of Lévi's report on his India/Japan mission of 1897-1898 and manuscripts for his Nepal monograph (1898-1905).
research_consequence: Distinct manuscript-authorial witness to the mission, potentially preserving wording/chronology absent from the published report.

documented_fact: Guide describes Sylvain Lévi papers: 3360 doctoral thesis manuscript; 3361 mission report and Nepal; 3362-3363 works 1907-1912; 3364-3365 miscellaneous manuscripts/notes; 3366 printed articles/proofs.
research_consequence: Do not collapse this scholarly-manuscript group into the looted private-correspondence archive or the Collège de France holdings.

documented_fact: Official report says Lévi was on mission and directed no conference during 1897-98; Finot maintained the teaching.
research_consequence: State mission dossier can now be used to refine the administrative chronology behind this full-year teaching interruption.

documented_fact: Lévi is back; regular conferences are Bhagavad-Gītā and a continuous survey of Indian literature. Stickney is an active participant. No regular Pāli-Buddhism course appears here.
research_consequence: Confirms realized teaching after the mission; remains separate from individualized/private reading.

documented_fact: The report explicitly says that outside the two regular conferences Lévi continued Bhagavad-Gītā reading with Stickney.
research_consequence: Direct primary proof that reported instruction could occur outside the regular conference programme. Strong modality control for the Lovejoy private-reading claim, not proof of the 1898 event.

documented_fact: Louis Finot formally advertises 'Explication de textes du canon pâli' and 'La littérature bouddhique'.
research_consequence: Shows Pāli canon and Buddhist literature could be explicit catalogue categories in the same Lévi-Finot institutional network; does not backdate this exact formal title to 1896-99.

documented_fact: Henri Maspero and Oger regularly came Tuesdays 5-7 to Lévi's home to prepare two Sanskrit-Chinese lexica under his direction.
research_consequence: Strong direct proof that home-based individual/small-group scholarly instruction formed part of Lévi's documented teaching practice; no retrojection to Lovejoy without letters.

documented_fact: From February, supplementary sessions with Dufresne compared two Chinese versions of the Questions of Menander with the Pāli Milinda-panha.
research_consequence: Confirms Pāli could appear in supplementary comparative textual work outside a simple regular-course label.

documented_fact: The IVe Section student/auditor list states 399 registrations for the two semesters and only prints auditors recognized by directors in their reports. Current indexed text search has not surfaced Lovejoy.
research_consequence: Do not infer Lovejoy did not attend Lévi. The list is selective by its own statement, and the searchable index may be incomplete.

documented_fact: Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot represented the EPHE at the Abel Bergaigne monument inauguration at Vimy on 9 Oct 1898.
research_consequence: This is a new hard public-presence date in France after the Asian mission, eight days before the first Wilson-cited Lovejoy Paris letter (17 Oct 1898). It sharply narrows Lévi's return-to-Paris institutional window without proving his exact Paris arrival day.
